PULMONOLOGY / OCCUPATIONAL LUNG DISEASE CLINIC E-CONSULT NOTE

Date/Time: 2024-06-03T15:00:00+00:00
Patient: Lenny Cummerata (DOB: 1955-12-31, Age: 68, Sex: Male)
MRN: SYN-9493155 (Patient ID: sr-305)
Requesting Clinician: Gideon Farrow-Achebe, MD (Internal Medicine / Primary Care)
Consulting Clinician: Evander Mukherjee-Solberg, MD (Pulmonology / Occupational Lung Disease Clinic)

REASON FOR E-CONSULT
Management of asbestosis with progressive exertional dyspnea (mMRC grade 2) and evaluation of the patient's request for a prolonged course of oral prednisone following a 5-day course prescribed at urgent care in February 2024.

1. CLINICAL HISTORY REVIEW

A. Occupational Exposure & Smoking History:
- Worked from 1972 to 1999 (27 years) as a pipe and boiler insulator and subsequently as a pipefitter in power plants and refineries.
- Directly mixed and applied asbestos-containing insulation without respiratory protection until the mid-1980s.
- Tobacco history: Lifelong never-smoker.
- Prior workers' compensation claim evaluated and documented in Occupational Medicine (2019-06-10).

B. Chest Imaging:
- Chest Radiograph (2019-06-10): Bilateral calcified pleural plaques; ILO profusion 0/1

GUI.final: COMPLETED: Reviewed the clinical history, chest HRCT, PFTs/6MWT, ABG, and all oximetry measurements for Lenny Cummerata (MRN SYN-9493155). Determined that prednisone is not indicated for fibrotic asbestosis and carries substantial risk. Identified severe exertional desaturation (nadir SpO2 86% on room air via reliable forehead-sensor 6MWT oximetry, contrasting with the unreliable cold-finger urgent care reading of 95%) that corrected to 92% with improved walk distance on 2 L/min pulsed oxygen. Assessment
1. Diagnosis & Clinical History:
68-year-old lifelong never-smoker male (MRN SYN-9493155) with confirmed asbestosis and asbestos-related pleural plaques.
- Occupational Exposure: Worked 1972-1999 (27 years) as a pipe/boiler insulator and pipefitter in power plants and refineries, mixing and applying asbestos-containing insulation without respiratory protection until the mid-1980s.
- Chest Imaging: 2019 CXR showed bilateral calcified pleural plaques (ILO 0/1). 2023-11-20 HRCT chest demonstrated bilateral calcified and non-calcified pleural plaques along the diaphragm and posterolateral chest wall, and basal-predominant subpleural reticulation with subpleural curvilinear lines and mild traction bronchiectasis (no honeycombing, ground-glass opacity, mass, or effusion), consistent with asbestosis.
- Pulmonary Function Testing (2024-05-14): Moderate restrictive ventilatory defect with FVC 66% predicted (68% in May 2023), FEV1/FVC 0.82, TLC 63% predicted, and moderately severe reduction in diffusing capacity (DLCO 46% predicted, down from 49% in May 2023, corrected for Hb 14.6 g/dL).
